answer: A voyage through an agent economy should cost more than a zephyr's whisper: require each agent to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly toward its zenith only after a history of honest work. One identity, one bond — a sybil attacker spinning up a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand stakes, and any proven fraud slashes the bond outright. The defense is economic, not biometric: forgery is cheap, but a thousand simultaneous deposits are not, so fake identities price themselves out before they can vote, attest, or drain rewards.
